title: Automated Code Generation for Lattice Quantum Chromodynamics and beyond
review_status: full-text audit complete; deterministic DSL/compiler with architecture-specific HPC evaluation, not AI-generated code
sections_checked: QIRAL language and generated OpenMP C workflow
algorithm composition and hot-kernel library specialization
iterative method and architecture performance results
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 submitted 2014-01-09; primary arXiv PDF audited.
evidence_note: QIRAL compiles a domain-specific scientific DSL into OpenMP C and uses hand-tuned/specialized libraries. It is competitive on several tested machines but >2x slower than tmLQCD on Nehalem-EX without SSE SIMD; architecture and full convergence time alter conclusions. One scientific domain, specific hardware/algorithms; not ML/LLM code generation.

title: Modeling Variability in Template-based Code Generators for Product Line Engineering
review_status: full-text audit complete; one industrial generator case comparing artifact structure, not AI generation
sections_checked: copy-paste versus layered generator variant construction
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 submitted 2016-06-09; proceedings version in Modellierung 2016.
evidence_note: For one generator with two variants, template LOC falls 7,823 to 6,231 (~80%); helper LOC falls 1,858 to 1,009 (~54%), or ~63% excluding unused copied helpers. DEFINE-block counts are comparable. Measures structural size only, not correctness, engineering time, defect rate, or general productivity. Traditional model-driven code-generator variability, not AI.

title: InverseCoder: Self-improving Instruction-Tuned Code LLMs with Inverse-Instruct
review_status: full-text audit complete; controlled gains on several benchmarks but model/benchmark cells are not uniformly improved
sections_checked: ablations, dataset scaling, self-consistency, and limitations
venue_year_verified: arXiv v2 dated 2024-12-16; sampled frame records version v2.
evidence_note: Generates 90,363 instruction pairs by code summarization and same-model YES/NO self-selection, then fine-tunes with original GPT-4-generated corpus. Pass@1 improves in many comparisons, but not every model/benchmark/library cell (e.g. CodeLlama-Python-7B DS-1000 average 40.2 to 39.9). Multiple instructions per response can hurt; repeated rounds do not significantly improve. Not independent of the original GPT-4-generated corpus; evaluation is benchmark-level, not repo-level correctness.

title: SWE-Refactor: A Repository-Level Benchmark for Real-World LLM-Based Code Refactoring
review_status: full-text audit complete; 18-project Java benchmark with joint behavior and requested-refactoring verification
sections_checked: compilation/test plus AST transformation success criteria
evidence_note: 1,099 Java examples from 18 projects; compound cases are harder than atomic. GPT-5.1-Codex succeeds on 151/200 in its reported subset, including 13/33 compound (39.4%); do not mistake the latter denominator for all 177 compound examples. Joint test/compile and AST-based intended-refactor verification is stricter than compile/test alone. Java and method-level scope; benchmark and model snapshot limit transfer.
